The `SimpleThemeToggle.astro` component contains the SVG for the icons.

The light mode icon (which is displayed when the theme is dark, to switch *to* light mode) is the **moon icon**:

```html
  <svg class="moon-icon" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="18" height="18" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2.5">
    <path d="M21 12.79A9 9 0 1 1 11.21 3 7 7 0 0 0 21 12.79z"></path>
  </svg>
```
This SVG draws a crescent moon.

Conversely, the dark mode icon (displayed when the theme is light, to switch *to* dark mode) is the **sun icon**:
```html
  <svg class="sun-icon" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2.0">
    <circle cx="12" cy="12" r="5"></circle>
    <line x1="12" y1="1" x2="12" y2="3"></line>
    <line x1="12" y1="21" x2="12" y2="23"></line>
    <line x1="4.22" y1="4.22" x2="5.64" y2="5.64"></line>
    <line x1="18.36" y1="18.36" x2="19.78" y2="19.78"></line>
    <line x1="1" y1="12" x2="3" y2="12"></line>
    <line x1="21" y1="12" x2="23" y2="12"></line>
    <line x1="4.22" y1="19.78" x2="5.64" y2="18.36"></line>
    <line x1="18.36" y1="5.64" x2="19.78" y2="4.22"></line>
  </svg>
```
This SVG draws a circle with lines radiating from it, representing the sun.

The visibility of these icons is controlled by CSS:
```css
  [data-theme='light'] .sun-icon {
    display: none; /* Hide sun when light theme is active */
  }

  [data-theme='dark'] .moon-icon {
    display: none; /* Hide moon when dark theme is active */
  }
```
So, when it's light mode, the `.sun-icon` (which would switch to dark mode) is hidden, and the `.moon-icon` (which would switch to light mode) is shown. However, the user specifically asked for the "light mode icon". This can be interpreted in two ways:
1.  The icon *representing* light mode (the sun).
2.  The icon you click to *activate* light mode (the moon, shown when in dark mode).

Given the phrasing, the user is most likely asking for the icon that *represents* light mode itself. That would be the **sun icon**. If they meant the icon to *switch to* light mode, that would be the moon icon.

To be precise:
*   The **sun icon** is used on the button when the site is in **dark mode**, and clicking it switches to **light mode**.
*   The **moon icon** is used on the button when the site is in **light mode**, and clicking it switches to **dark mode**.

Therefore, the icon that visually represents "light mode" is the sun.
